question:
Consider the function $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x-1}{3}\right)$.

(a) Determine the domain and range of $f$.

(b) Find all values of $x$ for which $f(x)=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

(c) Solve the inequality $f(x)\leq0$, subject to the domain of the function.
explanation:
(a)
For the inverse sine function to be defined,
$$-1\leq\frac{2x-1}{3}\leq1$$
Multiplying throughout by $3$,
$$-3\leq2x-1\leq3$$
Adding $1$ and dividing by $2$ gives
$$-1\leq x\leq2$$
Therefore, the domain is $[-1,2]$. As the argument assumes every value in $[-1,1]$, the range is
$$\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$$

(b)
Given that
$$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2x-1}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}$$
taking sine on both sides gives
$$\frac{2x-1}{3}=\frac{1}{2}$$
Therefore,
$$4x-2=3$$
$$x=\frac{5}{4}$$
This value belongs to $[-1,2]$. Hence, $x=\dfrac{5}{4}$.

(c)
The function $\sin^{-1}t$ is increasing and satisfies $\sin^{-1}t\leq0$ when $t\leq0$. Therefore,
$$\frac{2x-1}{3}\leq0$$
$$x\leq\frac{1}{2}$$
Combining this with the domain $[-1,2]$, the solution is
$$x\in\left[-1,\frac{1}{2}\right]$$
